text:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — we're seeing a few kv-cache prefetch errors show up in customer-facing routes (acme/org=acme, model=gpt-mini) across eu-west and us-west regions. Can someone point me to a saved search or dashboard that filters by org/model/route/region/status?

Ben Ortiz: for quick hunting use the LogSearch view `kv-prefetch-ops` (Saved searches -> Observability -> kv-prefetch-ops). It has org/model/route tags. Try adding `region:` to narrow it.

Samir Patel: If you don't have the saved view, here's a tight query I run:
```
service:inference OR service:runtime
json.request.headers.org:"acme" AND json.model.name:"gpt-mini"
route.name:/generate/* AND tag.region:(eu-west OR us-west)
level:warning OR level:error
message:*kv_cache*prefetch*
```
That returns prefetch attempts and failures.

Maria Chen: awesome, thx. Any guidance on filtering by HTTP status or internal error codes?

Rachel K: append `http.status_code:[500 TO 599]` for server errors. For our internal prefetch error codes we log `prefetch.err_code` in the JSON payload — e.g. `prefetch.err_code:1003` is timeout.

Jiayi Wu: FWIW ops-bot alert recently spiked on that route at 02:13 UTC. ops-bot: can you paste the alert link?

ops-bot: Alert: kv-prefetch-failure-rate high — https://monitoring.redwood.com/alerts/kv-prefetch-failure-rate (alert id: A-7782). Triggered rules: "kv_prefetch_rate_by_route" threshold 0.06.

Ben Ortiz: If you want a per-org breakdown, add `group_by: json.request.headers.org, route.name` in the query UI or use the dashboard metric `kv_prefetch.rate_by_org_route` (Dashboards -> Inference -> KV Prefetch).

Samir Patel: Also helpful: saved search `ops/kv-prefetch-by-region` includes pre-set tokenization for `env:prod` and `route.env` so you can swap org quickly.

Maria Chen: Can someone paste a minimal LogSearch snippet to find 5xx + prefetch.err_code 1003 in eu-west for acme?

Rachel K: Sure — paste this into logsearch: 
```
service:runtime
json.request.headers.org:"acme"
json.model.name:"gpt-mini"
tag.region:eu-west
http.status_code:[500 TO 599]
json.prefetch.err_code:1003
| sort by @timestamp desc | limit 100
```
Should show the recent failures.

Jiayi Wu: For trace links, logs include `trace_id` in `json.trace.id` — click the trace link column in the saved view. If you want a quick pivot to traces: use the dashboard tile "Prefetch failures -> Trace links".

Maria Chen: Great. One more — if I want to create a saved search that other SREs can reuse, what's the naming convention?

Ben Ortiz: Prefix with the team path: `eng-sre/kv/prefetch-acme-eu` then add tags `type:search, owner:@maria`. Keep it under Observability -> Saved searches.

Samir Patel: Also add a short description in the saved search metadata: what it filters and recommended time range (e.g., last 24h).

Maria Chen: I'll create `eng-sre/kv/prefetch-acme-eu` and link it in the incident ticket. Will tag @Ben for review.

Ben Ortiz: :thumbsup: ping me when it's created and I'll add the dashboard tile.

Rachel K: Optional: if you want an automated alert tweak, we can lower the threshold for that specific route in eu-west to 0.04 for a 15m window and see noise. I'll draft a PR to alerting-config.

Jiayi Wu: Noted — if we tweak, let's add suppression for controlled canaries.

Maria Chen: Thanks team — this is enough to proceed. I'll post the saved-search link once done.

Ben Ortiz: FYI for future: common filters we use for these are `json.request.headers.org`, `json.model.name`, `route.name`, `tag.region`, `http.status_code`, `json.prefetch.err_code`. Keeping those as columns in the saved view makes triage faster.

ops-bot: Deployment: rollout/kv-cache-prefetch-fix v2.1 started by @rachel at 2026-03-17T02:35:00Z.

Maria Chen: noted — thanks, closing loop. :white_check_mark:
